thrust_v09.note: v0.9 sim plant round (architect decisions b, d; 2026-10-28). THRUST IS UNKNOWN: the bench supply could not reach full power and the seller's 3.09 kgf (thrust_nominal_N, a PROXY table at 22.2 V) is unverified. The VTOL plant flies T_max at 22.2 V from design_envelope_kgf_at_22v2 (2.14 = T/W 1.3 for the battery VTOL, .. 3.09 seller) and the stress band 1.9 .. 2.14 (exercises the take-off check); it replaces the old thrust_scale 0.80-1.25 VTOL sampling. Thrust ~ (V_esc / voltage_ref_V)^voltage_exponent_proxy (the proxy table's 22.2 -> 25.2 V ratio gives 1.61; a 6S pack at 3.7 V/cell loaded at full throttle (18 mOhm, ~20.4 V) gives end_of_pack_thrust_factor 0.87, sizing/vtol_sizing.py). Electrical power P = power_nominal_W (T / T_ref)^power_exponent, P1 T_ref = thrust_nominal_N (proxy efficiency), P2 T_ref = the plant's T_max (pessimistic) - sim/tether.py FanPower. Rotor: omega(T) = KV voltage_nominal_V 2 pi / 60 sqrt(T / T_max_22V2) (no-load speed at T_max ASSUMED: an upper bound), angular momentum -s I omega z_b with I = rotor_inertia_kg_m2_ASSUMED (fan + motor bell, not measured): gyroscopic moment -w x h and the spool-up reaction +s I domega/dt on the body (sim/edf.py RotorModel). The controllers keep the params model (thrust_nominal_N, no voltage term); only the plant changes. Measure thrust, current, V_esc and rpm on the flight LiPo before flight.

bundle.note: PHOTOS 2026-10-29 (ASSUMED, read off the photos): the three leads are bundled in black heat-shrink from the motor exit, run as ONE bundle radially out along / behind one stator vane and under the rear rim; after the heat-shrink they are single red / blue / black silicone leads (long stock leads). FIX ROUND (reviews 2026-10-29): the FACTORY sleeve is not used as it is. The photos show it ending at about the housing's outer surface at the rim (r ~49, ~31 mm from the can; FIND-M2), stepped (two layers, the outer ~20 % thicker; G5), with the three leads leaving it stacked along the motor axis (G3 / FIND-M1: a ribbon of unknown orientation). With the triangle -> row transition the leads need before the bend (Layout.ml_transition_len, E) a 28-31 mm sleeve does not fit (Layout raises: rim corner). ASSEMBLY STEP (spec, not a reading): slit and remove the factory outer sleeve(s) - only if they do not cover the winding-to-lead joints (measure / look first; if they do, STOP: the notch must be re-designed) - and re-sleeve the first shrink_len_from_motor_ASSUMED = 14 +- 1 mm from the can surface with ONE layer of heat-shrink over the three leads laid in a triangle (round). od_ASSUMED 8.4 = three O3.6 leads in a triangle (1 + 2/sqrt 3) x 3.6 = 7.76 + 2 x 0.3 shrink wall (E) is therefore the re-sleeve target, not a photo reading (with the 14 mm sleeve the bundle ends inside the duct (r 31.65) and never enters the notch; Layout builds up to 11.6, review probe for the old 28 mm sleeve: 9.0 -> 0 mm^3, 9.6 -> 0.95 mm^3). After the sleeve, the leads go from the triangle to a row SIDE BY SIDE ACROSS the slot (tangential: black / blue / red across, not stacked along the axis) over the straight run before the bend. Limits (Layout bisection, E): shrink length <= 19.87 mm (VTOL) / 20.65 (rocket) keeps shrink + transition before the bend (C29 WARNs beyond). gap_to_te_ASSUMED = the bundle's top under the stator trailing edge / rear rim face (filled by the RTV bead). shrink_g_ASSUMED 0.3 g (pi x 8.4 x 0.3 x 28 mm^3 x ~1.3 g/cm^3, kept for the 14 mm sleeve: conservative), lumped with the RTV.

jet_drag.note: v0.9 lead-exit, photo round (E): the heat-shrink BUNDLE crosses the EDF jet as one body O od behind the stator vane; drag D = Cd q A_f, A_f (Layout.ml_jet_drag) = bundle.od x (duct_r - hub radius) (inside the hub radius 20 = hub_d_ASSUMED / 2 it sits in the hub's shadow; single leads count x od only where the shrink ends inside duct_r), q = T / (2 A_exit) as in C33 / sizing. Cd 1.0 central, 0.8-1.2 band (ASSUMED): a circular cylinder at Re = V D / nu ~ 52 m/s x 8.4 mm / 1.5e-5 ~ 3e4 (subcritical, Cd ~1.0-1.2); the rounded-triangle section and the 2 mm vane directly ahead (an upstream plate lowers a cylinder's drag) are not credited. C33 adds the moment D x (centroid) to the CG trim; vtol_sizing derates the thrust for T/W 1.3 by D / T. Round 1 (three leads side by side + a bend off the can): A_f 309 mm^2. FIX ROUND (reviews 2026-10-29): with the 14 mm re-sleeve the round bundle runs from the hub radius to the shrink end and the single leads from there to duct_r are counted as a full row side by side (count x od broadside, conservative over the triangle -> row transition): A_f 210 -> 242 mm^2. Cd band: the bodies in the jet are short (bundle span / OD ~1.9, row span / width ~0.9, one end on the hub / vane); for a flat plate normal to the flow Cd is ~1.2 up to aspect ratio ~5 (Hoerner) - the 2D value 2.0 applies to long plates only - so the 0.8-1.2 band also covers the row (FIND-M1's Cd 2.0 case is a 2D ribbon). C33 takes its status from the band's worst end (G4). Bench thrust: the factory routing already has the leads in the jet, so a bench thrust of THIS unit as built includes the drag - the T/W derate (vtol_sizing) applies only to thrust that does not come from such a test (the proxy table); the C33 moment term stays (FIND-M4).

lower_route.note: v0.9 lead-exit, PHOTO ROUND (user photos 2026-10-29, edf.wire_exit): the EDF-internal part of the route - motor side exit at the front ring (radial, heat-shrink bundle) -> straight behind ONE stator vane's trailing edge -> under the housing's rear rim into the propulsion lead notch -> the single leads (after the shrink) bend 90 deg up the slot beside the housing. One bend only (round 1: three, with a 23 mm climb along the can - superseded). bend_r_centre_ASSUMED = the smallest centre-line bend radius of a single 12 AWG silicone lead (2 x od_ASSUMED; measure by bending a lead round a 14 mm rod). The bundle itself is not bent: after the re-sleeved shrink (14 mm, bundle.note) the leads go from the triangle to a tangential row over Layout.ml_transition_len (E: S-bend of offset od / sqrt 3 at radius bend_r_centre, 7.45 mm) before the bend (Layout.ml_shrink_bend_margin = bend start - (shrink end + transition); < 0 = the bundle / unformed leads take the first part of the bend, C29 WARNs; fix round 2026-10-29, G2 / G3). Restraint 'rtv_bond_stator_te' = the bundle bonded with silicone RTV to the stator vane's trailing edge along the straight run inside the vane's span (Layout.ml_bond_u; no cable tie round the vane - it would loop over the vane's leading edge next to the rotor); the bead bridges the gap from the bundle to the trailing edge (Layout.ml_stator_te_gap <= bond_gap_max_ASSUMED, else Layout raises). Free spans exit -> bond start and bond end -> notch <= max_free_span_jet_ASSUMED (40 mm carried over from the intake plenum - ASSUMED, open issue). rtv_g_ASSUMED: bond bead along ~25 mm of the bundle (round 1 0.4 g for 12.5 mm -> 0.8), the notch seal after installation (opening ~1.5 x round 1's: 0.5 -> 0.8) and Kapton chafe tape on the rim corner / notch edges, lumped into motor_leads at the notch with the bundle's heat-shrink. No printed strut. Lead lengths and masses: the whole route + slack is still counted (stock_len_in_edf_mass_ASSUMED 0).

The clock mount uses motor_leads.generosity_box; from here it keeps rtv_g_ASSUMED (bond optional but counted, chafe tape; the notch seal is replaced by lead_passage.top_plug_g_ASSUMED), bundle.shrink_g_ASSUMED, bond_gap_max_ASSUMED (C29 WARNs when TE inset + rim gap exceed it: thicker RTV bead or a shim), max_free_span_jet_ASSUMED and jet_drag (drag area of the WORST corner, E).

clock_keyways.note: wire09c clock mount (user 2026-10-30: 'make the lead passage generous, I do not want to measure'; judge concept C): the EDF is turned (clocked) until its factory lead bundle points into the ONE lead passage (lead_passage); its two tabs then drop into the nearest pair of keyways cut round the circle. The keyway angles are COMPUTED by Layout._clock_seat (never typed in): a keyway kw wide (takes tabs up to kw - 0.4 = 3.6 thick; tab t 3.0 stays ASSUMED) is placed where its sleeve teeth (sleeve_min) stay out of the passage, its walls web_margin off the webs, col_clear off the servo-lead column guide walls (col_wall, U channel beside each column) and off the joint holes, gaps <= 2 x E_cov_deg; a tab may also hover in the passage. Coverage (C34): any exit azimuth is within E_cov_deg of theta_P for some seat; the passage takes E_cov_deg + the tab's play. No tab screws / lugs. pad_t: the floor pad under every keyway bridges the sleeve and the skin (JUDGE FIX 1.2 -> 3.0: one tab at the 20 g touchdown gives a bending factor 1.2 at 1.2 mm, 7.6 at 3.0 (E)), with a 45 deg corbel underneath (prints without support). Fix round (review F1, 2026-11-04): a sleeve tooth between two keyways (or a keyway and the passage) is a free pillar sleeve_r - edf_bore_r deep from the keyway floor to the deck; it must carry the full design motor torque (C35's max(1, 1.5 P / omega)) on ONE tab, fixed-fixed, uniform load, bending factor >= tooth_factor_min against printer.bending_mpa (E) - so every tooth is planned >= that width + tooth_w_margin (the 1.73 mm tooth beside the 193.55 deg hover-seat keyway had a factor ~0.6). The planner is a seat chain on the mod-180 circle (plan_step_deg grid): consecutive seats >= the tooth spacing and <= 2 E_cov_deg - plan_gap_margin_deg apart (coverage margin), fewest seats, then the smallest largest gap. C35 measures the teeth on the solid.

lead_passage.theta_note: theta_deg 0 = today's ESC (+x) side: the intake groove, bulkhead hole, bay route and servo gather stay. 180 is the user's alternative - a user decision, not the default. The judge's 'every configuration PASSes C33 at 180' is NOT reproduced (docs/v0.9_하드웨어_변경.md 17.10, E): with the whole lead route mirrored to -x and the leads up to +8.9 g longer, battery gets worse (11.8 %) and tether / hybrid stay above 10 %; at 180 the bay's bullet joint also meets the tether bus clamp (Layout refuses it). The recommended C33 fix is a CG shift toward -x (17.10).
lead_passage.note: wire09c clock mount: ONE lead passage ('fan') through the propulsion module at theta_deg - in plan the union of radial rectangles from duct_r - u_start_below_duct to r_wall, half width = the largest tangential envelope half of motor_leads.generosity_box + fan_margin, turned over +-(E_cov_deg + tab play); r_wall = motor_d / 2 + the longest factory sleeve + the largest bend radius + the thickest leads stacked + bend_tol (Layout._clock_fan, about 75.5 mm: OUTSIDE the 60 mm body - two independent concept studies proved no route inside r 60 takes a 24-35 mm factory sleeve or R 15). The passage leaves the body through a BLISTER (the fan grown by wall, from floor_margin + wall under the lowest lead envelope up to blister_top_gap under the intake) with a 45 deg V keel under its floor (keel_step mm steps, prints upright without support). Assembly (fix round, review F3): bend the single leads up ~90 deg BEFORE lowering the EDF (any radius 7-15), turn the EDF until the bundle points into the passage and lower it with the leads standing in the passage, push the vertical part out against the outer wall (within ~4 mm of it in a hover seat), lay them flat at u_top in the intake groove (the steer runs steer_len up to z_top_gap under the intake). top_plug_g_ASSUMED: closed-cell foam plug round the leads at the passage top (blocks jet -> intake recirculation; the servo foam pad material). It replaces the 22 mm slot box, the 12.4 mm lead notch (wire_slot.low_*) and the tab screws / lugs when tab_mount = 'clock_keyways'. Fix round (review F8): the foam plug fills the open blister top outside r 60 round the leads (about 530 mm^2, 250 mm^2 outside the intake groove walls).

coupler.note: printed vane_coupler (class D): hub with a D-bore (vane shaft_d + bore_clearance_dia, flat matching vane.d_flat_depth, facing vane_drive.flat_side) on the vane shaft's D-flat, locked by set_screw; the flange (D flange_d) is a socket for the stock MG90S double-arm horn (socket). Torque only: the vane's side load goes into the hinge bushing in the boss; axially the vane + coupler are retained between the boss face (boss_gap) and the duct wall and never touch the horn (v0.9 fix round (2026-10-28, reviewer defects); v0.9 CAD-1 had 2 x M2 x 4 screws into a horn trimmed to a disc, which has no room - reviewer)

socket.note: v0.9 fix round (2026-10-28, reviewer defects) (reviewer: 'coupler-to-horn fastening has no room'): the flange is a SOCKET for the stock horn - a slot through the flange (open at both ends along the horn arms, width = horn arm_w_ASSUMED + slot_fit, from the hub end face to over_arm_plane past the horn's arm plane, with a relief of horn collar_d + collar_relief_dia for the horn's round hub at the arm level and its spline collar). slot_fit 0.05 = print, then hand-fit the slot to the arms (each 0.1 mm of fit is ~1 deg of vane play peak to peak). Torque goes through the arm flanks (no screws); the arms can slide along the slot (they lie along v at neutral, the direction the foam pad pushes the servo), so the coupler takes no side load. The slot floor stays horn_axial_gap short of the arm face so the coupler never pushes the horn axially

Above the case: a connector bay (MG90S lead cut to servo_leads.fin_route.servo_lead_kept_ASSUMED + an inline 3-pin connector, connector_lwh_ASSUMED = length (radial) x width x height of the mated pair) so the servo comes out without cutting the lead. The fin plate passes through the fairing (the pocket cuts it) and continues above and outboard of it unchanged: the fins stay the landing legs (footprint unchanged).

vtol.timing_note: alt_max_m 20 -> 12 (2026-10-20, found by the reference agent) -> 10 (v0.7.1: the 6-DOF landing from 12 m took 27.0 s from V2 to LANDED - reference lag, ground 0.11 m below the pad, 3.6 s touchdown confirmation - leaving 3.0 s before the V6 hard cutoff; from 10 m the margin is ~6 s more): the flight-time LAND starts at max_flight_s - land_reserve_s = 30 s and the hard cutoff is at hard_cutoff_s = 60 s, so a landing from alt_max_m must take < 30 s: (12 - flare 1) / 0.6 + 1 / 0.3 + landed_confirm 0.5 = 22.2 s (7.8 s margin); from 20 m it took 35.5 s. Flight time is CUMULATIVE motor time since boot (one pack, no recharge between hops; a power cycle = a new pack resets it). Arm switch opened in LANDED -> SAFE (no release toward a person handling the landed vehicle); the take-off gate re-checks tilt and cell voltage at the end of the spool warning (both architect-approved 2026-10-20)
vtol.note: v0.7 VTOL mission (SPEC 8.9). ON (SAFE, every v0.4 ARM gate + the telemetry nonce) -> ARMED with a spool_warning_s buzzer warning -> POWERED: climb at climb_rate_mps to hover_altitude_m and hold it; UP / DOWN move the altitude target by alt_step_m within [alt_min_m, alt_max_m]; OFF -> land where it is (descent_rate_mps, touchdown_rate_mps below flare_altitude_m), touchdown confirmed for landed_confirm_s -> motor off (UNPOWERED) -> SAFE after safe_after_landed_s. Safety (the architect's design, user-approved 2026-10-20): link loss for link_loss_land_s -> land (a parachute cannot open from a few metres); flight time max_flight_s - land_reserve_s, low cell voltage, ceiling_m or a baro failure -> land (baro failure: on the inertial vertical speed); tilt > tilt_abort_deg, tilt / spin rate, IMU or NAV failure, a fall (v_z <= fall_vz_mps for fall_confirm_s), altitude > geofence_m, still powered at hard_cutoff_s, KILL or the arm switch opening -> ABORT (motor off now, release after abort_release_delay_s). Altitude / vertical-speed controller on the FCU (250 Hz): h_ref rate-limited towards the target, v_z command = alt_kp (h_ref - h) limited to [-vz_max_down_mps, vz_max_up_mps], throttle = hover feed-forward / cos(tilt) + vz_kp e_vz + vz_ki int(e_vz) within [u_min, u_max]. gains_ASSUMED are starting values for the simulation tuning (SPEC 9) v0.7.1 (architect, 2026-10-20): VTOL estimator nav_estimator, touchdown detector v2 + LAND floor timeout (touchdown), baro-failure bias state + time limit (baro_lost), LANDED rules (landed_rules_note), reference-rate feed-forward, baro thrust compensation, build profiles field / demo, alt_max_m 10. v0.8: GPS position hold (position_hold), NAV publish-then-correct ordering (flight_computer.nav.schedule_note).

vtol.land_ref_rebase_note: v0.9 fix round (control review HIGH 1 follow-up; sim.vertical_ctrl docstring 1c): entering LAND the reference becomes max(ref, h) - a power rule acting in the climb (W_LOST 1 s after the lift-off) otherwise started the descent 0.7 m below the climbing vehicle and the error asked for vz_max_down at the ground (P_H_unplug_climb 1.41 m/s).
vtol.nav_throttle_lagged_note: v0.9 fix round WHAT-IF (not adopted: TUNE overshoot 0.54 -> 0.60 m): the FCU would send its thrust-lagged throttle in the nlink thr_q byte the NAV's baro compensation uses.

nav_estimator.note: v0.7.1 VTOL NAV attitude estimator (the v0.6.3 pad-alignment + gyro-only estimator drifted 7.6 deg over a 40 s hover in the 6-DOF with the ASSUMED MPU-6050 bias wander: the vehicle held a wrong vertical and landed 7.7 m/s sideways, 120 m away; 0/20 campaign runs passed). Pad: unchanged alignment (gyro bias average + accelerometer levelling). Flight: quaternion integration of (gyro - b_hat) plus a Mahony correction kp * e, e = a_lpf_hat x up_hat_body (accelerometer low-passed at accel_lpf_hz, used only while | |a| - g | / g < accel_gate), and in-flight bias learning b_hat -= ki * e * dt bounded by bias_limit_dps per axis. Why it can work in a hover although the accelerometer mostly sees the thrust axis: an un-accelerated vehicle carries its weight with thrust + drag, so the averaged specific force points up in the world and reveals the tilt; a tilt error makes the vehicle accelerate until the momentum (ram) drag of the EDF intake flow and the cross-flow drag of the body balance it, so the time constant 1 / kp must be longer than that drag time constant (m / (dD/dv), several seconds). The 6-DOF must model both drags for this to be judged honestly (aero.vtol_*). Ballistic build: the v0.6.3 estimator, bit-identical. Yaw is not observable (no magnetometer) and is not corrected.

touchdown.release_note: v0.9 fix round (physics review medium 3, ground effect: the exit plane is the contact plane): in LAND, in the flare band, while the vehicle stands still and does not follow the descending reference ('still' unconfirmed), the throttle bias falls at release_per_s to -release_max (sim.vertical_ctrl docstring 5b); 'still' confirms only with the release complete. With the sampled ground effect (ASSUMED shape) 37 of 99 TUNE landings were confirmed while floating 3-12 cm up (drop 0.6-1.06 m/s); with the release 0 of 99 (80 confirm by support). Values ASSUMED; the hardware fix is landing feet (exit >= 45 mm above the contact plane, CAD request).
touchdown.note: v0.7.1 touchdown detector v2 (the v0.7.0 test |v_z| <= 0.15 m/s for 0.5 s was below the NAV v_z noise: touchdown never confirmed in 5/20 campaign runs, the motor then ran on the ground to the V6 cutoff, whose ABORT fired the release on the ground). Signatures, any one confirmed for landed_confirm_s while LAND and low (h <= flare_altitude_m, or the altitude loop saturated downward): (a) still - the old test on a filtered v_z; (b) support - the measured body-z specific force exceeds the free-flight value of the commanded thrust (T(u) / m) by more than support_g * g: something other than the fan carries the vehicle; (c) floor - the vertical controller sits at u_min (sat = -1) for floor_s: free flight cannot sustain T(u_min) < m g. LAND floor timeout: once the vehicle has been low in LAND for land_floor_timeout_s without a confirmed touchdown, the motor stops and the phase goes LANDED (motor off, NO release: a vehicle 0-1 m above the ground is safer with the fan stopped than with a release at the ground crew). ARCHITECT 2026-10-20 23:10 (after the reference study, sim/vertical_ctrl.py docstring 4-5): approved - still needs the reference lead alt_kp (h_ref - h) <= -2 touchdown_rate (0.48 m) and a 1.0 s low-pass on v_z, gated by h <= flare only; the baro-lost LAND flies the descending-reference law on the dead-reckoned h at descent_rate (no flare); pad accelerometer-bias running mean; altitude-filter bias pole 40 s (ASSUMED). Changed - floor = the loop pinned downward (u at u_min, OR the integrator at -vz_i_max with v_cmd at -vz_max_down) for floor_s, because with the tuned gains u cannot reach u_min on the ground; the LAND floor timeout counts only while low AND the reference has run that lead below the vehicle (not following it down), so a landing into ground below the pad level (a ditch) is not cut in the air (v0.7.0 rule: motor stopped 0.7 m up over ground 1.5 m below the pad).
touchdown.gating_v071b: architect 2026-10-21 03:05: no signature may stop the motor at altitude on the strength of the loop being saturated. still, floor and the V10 LAND floor timeout count only while h <= flare_altitude_m (low_alt); above it (ground above the pad / a baro offset) a touchdown needs support AND floor confirmed together; ground_signature for the baro-lost V8 rule unchanged.

baro_lost.note: v0.7.1 baro-failure landing (v0.7.0: the inertial v_z integrated the ASSUMED 10 mg accelerometer bias, 7/20 seeds flew away up to 147 m until V6). (1) The VTOL altitude filter carries an accelerometer z-bias state learnt while the baro is healthy (ballistic build: the v0.6.3 filter, bit-identical). (2) A time limit from the baro loss: T_lim = time_limit_factor * (h_at_loss / descent_rate_mps + flare_altitude_m / touchdown_rate_mps) + time_limit_margin_s; at T_lim a ground signature ((b) or (c) of touchdown) -> LANDED, else ABORT (motor off, release after abort_release_delay_s - the altitude is unknown, the vehicle may be high).

vtol.landed_rules_note: v0.7.1: in LANDED (motor already off) an I9 IMU/NAV failure, the geofence or the fall rule goes to SAFE, never ABORT: no release toward people handling a landed vehicle. KILL and the arm switch keep their meaning.
vtol.fcu_tick_order_note: v0.7.1 VTOL FCU tick order (architect, after the v0.7 integration measurements: supervisor + vertical controller cost 741-796 us BEFORE the attitude controller, so sample -> vane PWM reached 5.15 ms in the co-simulation vs 4.66 ms ballistic and the 6-DOF's 4.71 ms, and the NAV-tick -> vanes path exceeded one 4 ms tick): (1) attitude controller with this tick's NAV frame and the PREVIOUS tick's supervisor outputs and throttle u (gain schedule) -> (2) vane registers -> (3) supervisor -> (4) vertical controller -> (5) ESC register. Consequences: the vane path costs what it costs in the ballistic build; a supervisor decision reaches the ESC in the same tick and the vanes one tick (4 ms) later; the gain schedule sees u one tick old (thrust lag 0.15 s, ESC frames 50 Hz: immaterial). The ballistic order (supervisor -> attitude -> outputs) is unchanged. Also: the vertical controller's cos(tilt) comes from the NAV quaternion (1 - 2 (qx^2 + qy^2)), no cosf; u_ff = u_hover / sqrt(c) for throttle_exponent 2; reciprocals precomputed.
vtol.vz_ref_feedforward_note: v0.7.1: v_cmd = dh_ref/dt + alt_kp (h_ref - h): the rate of the rate-limited reference is fed forward, removing the ~climb_rate / alt_kp ramp lag (0.96 m peak on UP) that dominated the hold RMS in v0.7.0
vtol.baro_thrust_comp_note: v0.7.1: static-pressure error of the MS5611 with the fan running, as an altitude [m] at hover thrust (positive = the baro reads high, e.g. the electronics bay vented to the intake plenum), scaled with the commanded thrust T(u) / (m g). 0.0 = not calibrated. Measure it on the tether before the first free flight (build guide): hover tethered at a known height, compare h with a tape. The 6-DOF draws the true value as a plant variable (uncalibrated 0..1.5 m, calibrated residual)

thrust_learning.note: v0.7.1b (architect 2026-10-21 03:05, after the independent physics review: with a plant ~20 % stronger than the thrust model - the proxy table gives +23 % on a fresh 25.2 V pack - the loop could not follow the LAND reference down, sat pinned, and the floor / support signatures confirmed a touchdown at 6-8 m: motor stop, 10-12 m/s impact). The vertical controller learns the thrust ratio k_T = T_actual / T_model in free flight: k += (1 - exp(-dt / tau)) (f_z / (g r_thr) - k), clamped to [k_min, k_max], while POWERED, after the take-off ramp, h > flare_altitude_m, tilt < max_tilt_deg and f_z finite; k = 1 at each take-off; frozen otherwise. f_z / (g r_thr) is the thrust per model thrust whatever the vertical acceleration (the specific force excludes gravity), and a constant z accelerometer bias is absorbed. k_T is used in the feed-forward (u_ff = u_hover / sqrt(k_T c) for n = 2) and in the support signature (d = f_z - g k_T r_thr). Learning never commands anything by itself.
thrust_learning.v09_note: v0.9 control round: k_min 0.7 -> 0.55. The plant / model thrust ratio over the v0.9 envelope is 0.60 (2.14 kgf at 22.2 V x 0.87 end of pack against the model's 3.09 kgf) ... 1.23 (3.09 kgf, fresh pack); the take-off thrust search (mission.vtol.takeoff_v09) lowers k_T on the pad and needs k_T 0.55 to reach u_max (u_ff = 0.73 / sqrt(0.55) = 0.98) so the take-off check V15 can act on a plant that cannot lift. V14 (k_T x T/W < 1.08) stays: on the battery vehicle k_T < 0.576 lands.

Prototype (scratch snapshot, 2,000+ runs): station keeping 0.6-0.7 m RMS (max ~2 m, mostly GPS wander) in calm / 3-8 m/s wind / swinging direction / gusts, 3 N s pushes back within 0.5 m in ~1.7 s, touchdown <= 0.5 m/s over the ground in 95 % of field runs; GPS off drifts 13-139 m.
position_hold.review_v08_decisions: architect 2026-10-21 ~12:20, from the independent prototype review (scratchpad v08/report_gps-hold-review.json; all MUST be implemented): (1) NAV GPS filter = fixed-gain 3-state filter per axis (precomputed gains + innovation gates for 5 Hz, a second gain set for the first ~10 s / after a reset, no covariance propagation), delayed-state buffer indexed by tick, epoch work split so no NAV tick exceeds its free time (measured prototype: 1.02 ms per 50 Hz step, 7.4 ms per epoch - too slow; fixed-gain: 0.56 / 0.64 ms); (2) FCU position loop trig-free (compare squares, sqrt only when a limit acts, a_lim cached on k_T change, atan series, heading cos/sin from the NAV) and split into <= 0.2 ms background jobs; mind the FCU stack (966 B < 1024 B); (3) nlink keeps its 72 B frame: a 5 B ROTATING SLOT aligned with the NAV 50 Hz step carries px/py, vx/vy, reset delta, heading cos/sin (Q15), status (fix ok, ON-gate ok, reset counter, sats, accuracy class); (4) spin guard releases only with the estimated tilt within ~5 deg of the loop limit (tilt_guard_excess_deg 5) and no new tilt demand while the vertical controller is saturated high; tuning and validation on DIFFERENT seeds (fresh seeds showed a GPS-only I2 abort at 0.85 m); (5) wind envelope: operator limits field 6 m/s mean / gusts 8 m/s, demo 4 m/s; evaluate with near-ground turbulence intensity 0.2; touchdown policy in wind: tilt fades over the last ~0.3 m; (6) yaw: 1-state yaw Kalman update weighted by the information in each window (sigma ~ sigma_dv / |dv|), optional heading-alignment manoeuvre after the climb; (7) GPS-IMU plausibility rule -> GPS unusable -> attitude-only + LAND (tilt at its limit > ~3 s while |v| does not fall; |v_nav| > v_max + 1 m/s for 2 s; repeated resets); (8) UBX: match messages by iTOW, stamp epochs from a learned tick-to-iTOW offset, configure at 9600 and 38400 with ACK checks, poll MON-VER, gate on gpsFixOK + hAcc + sAcc + numSV; (9) quote station keeping as ~1 m RMS / 2.5 m max until a real module is measured (10 min static log on the pod with the EDF at hover throttle and LoRa transmitting; fit the error time constants into the sim).

Rule (a) counts a limited step ONLY in CLIMB/HOLD above flare_altitude_m, when the binding limit is the profile cap / authority with the vertical loop NOT saturated high, and the GPS velocity disagrees with the IMU-propagated velocity; rules (b), (c) and the fence keep catching runaways and velocity-bias faults.

touchdown_policy.note: architect 2026-10-21 21:00 after the v0.8 fix round (sim/out/vtol/v08_physreview_fix_studies.json): fading the tilt to 0 over the last 0.3 m let the wind push the vehicle sideways at touchdown - energy-method tip-over margin NEGATIVE in 8/20 demo runs at 4 m/s (ground speed p90 1.04 m/s); KEEPING the wind-trim tilt to touchdown gives 1/20 but leans > 5 deg in 10/20. The physical criterion is the tip-over margin (lean AND speed), so v0.8.1 keeps the trim: below the flare the position loop holds position with its trim tilt (no fade), only the transient part above the trim is limited; touchdown judged by tip_margin_mps > 0 (primary) and tilt <= trim + 5 deg (secondary). The v0.7 tilt <= 5 deg check applies to calm air only.

On the light VTOL vehicle (drag time constant 4.9 s) keep_trim let a wind change in the last 1-2 s carry the vehicle into the contact at 0.5-1.4 m/s (v0.9 criterion 0.3 m/s). TUNE seed 7400: touchdowns <= 0.3 m/s 55 -> 65 of ~100 landings, field_swirl passes 4 -> 7, no abort changed (scratch v09sim/control/changes.json). keep_trim and fade stay as comparison builds.

power_rules_ASSUMED.note: v0.9 power / tether round (sim.onboard docstring 'v0.9 power rules', codes and the proposed TELEM v4 / v5 power tail sim.power_link; thresholds from docs/tether_power_proposal.json firmware.rules_ASSUMED_thresholds, checked on the TUNE seeds 7400 only: healthy tether / hybrid flights reached V_in 20.57 V and a buffer 3.69 V/cell at the lowest, take-off peaks h_est 2.66 m - no rule acted). The FCU's power build (battery | wired = params power.source 'tether' | wired_buffer = 'hybrid') is a build-time choice; the battery build keeps the v0.8.1 rules exactly. adc_v_per_count = power.electrical_plant_ASSUMED.adc_full_scale_v / 1024 (the PF0 divider, VBAT_V_PER_COUNT; V_tether / V_buffer use the same divider on two free ADC pins). Every voltage is filtered in Q4 ADC codes (y += (16 x - y) >> filter_shift, 32 ms) and compared with integer thresholds. W_ARM (ON and the V7 take-off gate): V_tether (wired: V_in) in [arm_v_tether_min, arm_v_tether_max] at idle, wired_buffer also the buffer rest in [arm_buffer_cell_min, arm_buffer_cell_max] V/cell (3.72: SOC ~0.24, the energy for a P2 landing from alt_max with margin; 3.92: above it the crossover current drains the buffer in the hover). W_LOST (wired_buffer): V_tether < lost_v_min or < V_buffer - lost_below_buffer_v for lost_persist_s -> LAND on the buffer (proposal W2: <= 0.1 s). W_SAG (wired): V_in < sag_v for sag_warn_s -> throttle ceiling frozen + UP refused, for sag_land_s -> LAND (released after sag_release_s above sag_v + sag_hyst_v; sag_land_s 2.0 -> 1.0 on the tuning set: the supply latches off 5 s after its current limit starts and the landing needs the rest). W_BUF: buffer < buf_low_cell_v per cell for buf_persist_s (under load) or below the landing reserve buf_reserve_cell_v for buf_reserve_s (the crossover drains it while tethered) -> LAND. W_D2: buffer > d2_cell_v per cell while tethered for d2_persist_s -> LAND (D2 short: the tether charging the buffer). A power rule before the take-off check passed -> motor off, SAFE (like V15). I8 maps to the buffer (wired_buffer) and is replaced by W_SAG (wired). tether_limits (the smaller of these and the profile's): alt_max 2.0 m (UP refused above); ceiling / geofence 3.2 / 3.6 m sit above the take-off overshoot of the present vertical loop (up to ~1.2 m on the strong light tether vehicle, TUNE) - with them the overhead pulley must be >= 4.5 m above the ground (vehicle top = exit plane + 0.585 m, cable boot + 0.1 m); a 3.5-4.0 m gantry needs the take-off overshoot fixed first (control round). tether_endurance replaces the battery's flight time (no pack: conductor and motor heating, proposal V2_endurance 180 s). Known limit: a supply that current-limits on a short route keeps the bus near V_set - I_lim R_loop (> sag_v): the vehicle cannot see it (procedure: hover current <= 0.7 x the supply limit). ASSUMED until the tether bench test measures the route's voltage drop, the supply's limit behaviour and the buffer's sag.

vtol_overrides.v09fix_note: v0.9 fix round (2026-10-28, independent reviews; TUNE 7400 only, scratch v09sim/fix): att_err_mode 1 -> 2 (the reduced attitude error also without a tilt setpoint: TUNE swirl aborts 7 -> 6 with the rest), ff_rotor_gyro 1 -> 0 (the gyroscopic decoupling made the negative-swirl / vane-spread plants worse: swirl group aborts 12 -> 7 off), mix_yaw_trim_reserve 1 (new: when pitch / roll saturate the mixer it keeps the yaw integrator's trim share of d_z and drops only the transient yaw - the dropped trim let the residual swirl spin the body; I3 -> I2 in the physically saturated cases), ff_rotor_react kept 1 (a gain now; 0.5 / 0 tried, no gain). The control round's numbers stay in v09_note.
vtol_overrides.v09_note: v0.9 control round (VTOL hardware: the 1.40-1.65 kg VTOL vehicles, I_xx 0.029-0.035 / I_zz 0.0032 kg m2 instead of 0.132 / 0.0050; direct-drive vanes with ~1.65 deg of play; EDF rotor gyroscopic and spool-up torques). The VTOL build flies these on top of sim/out/gains.json (the ballistic gains, unchanged): rate_kp/ki/kd_xy and rate_kp/ki_z scaled by the inertia ratio (I_vtol / I_rocket: 0.266 pitch/roll, 0.647 yaw) - the v0.8.1 gains gave the light vehicle a 33 rad/s pitch crossover with 18 deg phase margin (4.5 deg at the strong end of the thrust envelope); att_err_mode 1 = the reduced attitude error while tilted (v0.8.2 candidate D); aw_per_axis 1 = per-axis conditional anti-windup (replaces the global 3-axis freeze); ff_rotor_* = rotor spool-reaction and gyroscopic feed-forwards (ff_rotor_h_nms = s x edf.thrust_v09.rotor_inertia_kg_m2_ASSUMED x edf.kv x edf.voltage_nominal_V x 2 pi / 60 with s = +1 for edf.rotation CW - regenerate when those change; VERIFY THE FAN'S ROTATION: a wrong sign doubles the torque instead of cancelling it); rate_i_max_z 0.25 kept (v0.7.1b). Evidence: scratch v09sim/control/changes.json; loop margins: v09sim/control/analysis/loops_final.json.

aero.vtol_aero_note: v0.7.1, VTOL 6-DOF only (the ballistic model stays bit-identical): (1) cross-flow drag of the body in a side wind, 1/2 rho V_perp^2 C_dc A_plan at the centroid of the body's side silhouette (A_plan = OD x length; C_dc ~ 1.2 for a circular cylinder at Re ~ 1e4-1e5), replacing the slender-body normal force for the VTOL runs; (2) EDF momentum (ram) drag mdot * V_rel_perp at the intake station, mdot = sqrt(rho A_exit T) (actuator disk); it is linear in the side speed and dominates at a few m/s, like rotor drag on a multirotor. Both set how far wind and pushes move the vehicle and are what makes the tilt observable to the NAV accelerometer in a hover

collar.plan_margin_note: the lever envelope in plan (lever Ø x tip sweep) lies inside the convex hull of the rim tops by >= this (A): then ANY plane that rests on the rim (an inverted set-down, a tip-over onto the top corner) stays over the rim height above the whole lever - a plane above every rim point is above the rim height over their convex hull. The notches cut the hull with a chord at |y| = sqrt(R_out^2 - (notch_w / 2)^2)
collar.lever_clear_note: lever envelope (every sampled throw angle) -> collar material, BRep distance (A): the lever never rubs the collar
collar.notch_note: two finger notches, one on each end of the throw axis. Review fix (2026-11-05, F1 / F2): each is a U slot across the wall - width notch_w, a round bottom of radius notch_w / 2 whose lowest point is notch_bottom_h over the plate top (centre notch_bottom_h + notch_w / 2 = 13.5 mm over the plate), straight sides above the centre up through the rim (was a 16 mm box slot from 5.4 mm). Why notches: in a closed Ø21 cup a fingertip cannot get to the outer side of the thrown lever tip (7.6 mm off the axis, 2.9 mm from the bore), so it could push the lever only one way; through a notch the fingertip comes in from the side and pushes the tip back over centre - both ways, one notch each. notch_w 17 = finger_tip_d_ASSUMED + 2 x finger_path_margin_min: the finger keeps 0.5 mm from the notch sides all along the push (finger_path_note). Why the U: the round bottom follows the round fingertip, so the slot is no deeper than the finger needs (the lowest point 5.0 mm keeps the sphere's lowest point in the wall band 0.87 mm over it, >= one layer, and the whole push >= 0.5 mm), and it removes the box slot's sharp re-entrant corners where the side-load stress peaked (kt_note). The unbroken base ring below (5.0 mm) keeps the arcs' bending root short (side_load) and the notches double as drains down to that height (the cup below them still holds ~5 mm of water round the outer nut: do not fly in rain - the bare switch had the same leak path)
collar.finger_path_note: review fix (2026-11-05, independent review F1: the end-position probe alone did not prove that the finger can push the lever back over centre; a 14 mm notch blocked the push and still passed): the fingertip probe (finger_tip_note) is kept on the lever's outboard tip corner (horizontal push, sphere centre level with the corner) while it pushes the lever from the end position to finger_path_past_centre_deg past centre, every finger_path_step_deg, and its distance to the collar material must stay >= finger_path_margin_min at every step (A: 0.5 mm side room each side for a real, soft fingertip; the old 16 mm notch had 0.000). Layout computes it (the U slot surface inside the wall, the plate) and refuses a short collar; C41 measures it on the solids (BRep). The governing step is near centre, where the finger body lies in the notch: room = notch_w / 2 - finger_tip_d / 2 = 0.5 mm (M/E)
collar.finger_tip_note: adult index fingertip modelled as a sphere Ø16 (A; the existing Ø20 finger circle = this fingertip + 2 mm each side). Finger-access rule (Layout, C41 on the solids): at each end position the sphere touches the outer corner of the lever's tip end with a horizontal push along the throw axis (the sphere centre level with that corner, finger_tip_d / 2 outboard of it), and the sphere plus the finger behind it (a Ø finger_tip_d cylinder 30 mm outward along the throw axis) meets no solid

side_load.kt_note: review fix (2026-11-05, F2): the box notch's sharp 90 deg corner at the notch bottom was the arc's most stressed fibre and sat on a layer boundary; the notch now has a round (U) bottom of radius notch_w / 2 = 8.5 mm, so the arc section grows smoothly below the U's centre and Layout searches the governing height (lp_col_section). A stress-concentration factor is still applied to that nominal stress (A, kt_notch 1.3: a shoulder with fillet radius / narrow width r/d ~ 1.6 (8.5 / ~5.1 mm) is below ~1.2 on Peterson's stepped flat bar in bending charts; rounded up for the layer lines crossing it). C41: factor = interlayer allowed / (kt x nominal) >= factor_min

plate_root.note: review fix (2026-11-05, F3): the 1.2 mm plate carries the collar's root moment and was not checked. Model (E, Layout lp_col_plate_root, cad/layout.py _annular_plate_boss): Kirchhoff annular plate, the collar a rigid boss (radius ro), clamped at b = the FARTHEST first support seen from the collar axis (rays every 1 deg to the rim ring's inner face, the hub and the four ribs - 50.6 mm here; the panel is really held at 11.5-19 mm on most sides, so this is conservative), nu 0.35 (A, PLA). Cases (C41): (1) the side load (F of the arc case) x rim height h as the boss moment; (2) an inverted set-down: the collar takes the lever-rule share body_r / (body_r + switch r) of the vehicle WITH the logic power x dyn, plus friction mu x that force on its rim (moment). The plate prints flat (layers in its plane), so allowed = printer.bending_mpa (in-layer flexural 53 MPa, the convention of sizing/vtol_strength.py which the C30 / C38 cap strength rule uses), factor >= factor_min; the factor against printer.tensile_mpa is reported too. Nominal stress: no root fillet / Kt (as vtol_strength)

side_load.note: hand estimate (E, C41): the whole vehicle WITH the logic power (report extra.logic_power.with_logic_power, M) x dyn 2 x friction 0.5 = the project's leg / ground case (sizing/vtol_strength.py DYN / MU, ASSUMED) pushed horizontally on the rim of ONE arc (an inverted set-down sliding on the floor); cantilever from the governing height of the U notch (review fix 2026-11-05, F2: Layout searches the arc section x arm along the notch, the arc = the annulus part outside the slot's half-width at that height, minimum Z, stress x kt_notch) and from the plate (full ring, arm h); the plate under the collar: plate_root; the cap prints top face up, so the bending stress crosses the layer lines: allowed = interlayer_fraction x printer.tensile_mpa (A, FDM Z strength ~40-60 % of in-layer), factor >= factor_min. Impact is not covered

gps_sky.note: no GPS elevation-mask rule existed (C30 only required the patch top to be the vehicle top except named exceptions). flight_computer.architecture: v0.6.3: three ATmega128A - NAV (MPU-6050 + MS5611 on I2C, attitude estimator, altitude filter, pad alignment; at the end of its 250 Hz tick it pushes the navigation frame to the FCU over the nlink SPI as the SPI master, SPEC 10.5), FCU (onboard supervisor I1-I10, attitude controller, PWM outputs, OpenLog log; SPI slave, its tick starts when a complete navigation frame has arrived) and COM (LoRa link, SPEC 10.4). Every flight computation runs on an ATmega128A
flight_computer.toolchain: avr-gcc (PlatformIO atmelavr, MegaCore ATmega128 board), C99; ported-to-CodeVisionAVR notes in firmware/README
flight_computer.fuses_note: M103C must be unprogrammed (ATmega103 compatibility mode is ON in new chips); JTAGEN unprogrammed to free PF4..PF7

nav.role: NAV: MPU-6050 + MS5611 (I2C 400 kHz via the 3.3 V level shifter), pad alignment / gyro-only attitude estimator, tilt, altitude filter, sensor health; at the end of every tick it pushes the navigation frame to the FCU as the nlink SPI master and receives the FCU's state bytes in the same exchange. No flight decisions: commands, interlocks, control and outputs stay on the FCU

pins.imu_int: PE6/INT6 (not used, polled at the tick)
pins.spi_ss: PB0 (output: FCU slave select, high = idle)
pins.spi_sck: PB1/SCK (output to FCU PB1; NAV ISP SCK)
pins.spi_mosi: PB2/MOSI (output: navigation frame to FCU PB2)

gps.note: v0.8: the NAV re-sends CFG-PRT / CFG-RATE / CFG-MSG / CFG-NAV5 at every boot (no flash save), parses UBX in a USART1 RX ring buffer (ISR) + background, fuses at 50 Hz with the GPS epoch update split over >= 4 ticks, compensates the 0.22 s latency (delayed-state) and the antenna lever arm. v0.8.1: MOVED to the GNS board (flight_computer.gns); the NAV USART1 now carries glink.

nav.schedule_note: v0.8 NAV tick order (architect 2026-10-21, after the v0.7.1 integration measured IMU -> vane 5.2 ms > 4.71 ms and NAV tick -> vane 4.7 ms > 4.0 ms): IMU read -> gyro prediction of the quaternion -> PUBLISH the nlink frame -> then the Mahony correction / bias learning, the VTOL altitude filter and the GPS fusion; their results enter the frame of the NEXT tick (a 4 ms delay on slow corrections).

com.role: COM: LoRa radio driver, uplink frame decoding (forwards decoded CMDs to the FCU), TELEM building from the FCU's reply snapshot, 1 Hz status to the FCU. No flight decisions: the onboard supervisor (commands, interlocks I1-I10) stays on the FCU

pins.ilink_rx: PE0/RXD0 (from FCU PD3/TXD1 through 1 kOhm; ISP PDI: unplug the ilink connector to program the COM)
pins.ilink_tx: PE1/TXD0 (to FCU PD2/RXD1, direct; ISP PDO)
pins.link_uart_tx: PD3/TXD1 (to module RXD through a BSS138 channel)

ilink.note: FCU USART1 <-> COM USART0, 8N1, U2X = 0 (UBRR 3: 0 % error at 16 MHz). Frame 0xC5 0x5C LEN TYPE payload CRC16-CCITT-FALSE (SPEC 10.4). Both boards on the 5 V logic UBEC, common ground

nlink.note: NAV = SPI master (fosc/8 = 2 MHz, mode 0, MSB first) -> FCU = SPI slave (interrupt per byte); one fixed-length full-duplex exchange per NAV tick, pushed when the navigation state is ready; byte_gap_us between bytes gives the FCU's slave interrupt time to load its next return byte (SPEC 10.5, src/core/nlink_proto.h). (v0.6.3 co-simulation: the NAV frame time moves by up to 0.45 ms at the pad -> flight switch; a fallback tick that starts later than ~4.6 ms leaves the FCU background no time and drops flight records (A/B: 4.6 ms 0 dropped, 4.7 ms 1, 5.0 ms 2-4), so frame_timeout_ms = 4.6 keeps 0.15 ms of margin on both sides.) If no complete frame arrives within frame_timeout_ms of the previous tick the FCU runs the tick on its own Timer2 with the navigation data invalid (imu_ok = baro_ok = false -> I9 after the supervisor's failure time)
nlink.exchange_watchdog_note: v0.9 firmware round (fw09/spec W1): the NAV master's interrupt-paced exchange (72 Timer3 compare-B interrupts, ~632 us on the chip; measured SS low 618-621 us in single-chip simavr, 636-641 us in the 4-core co-sim with the interrupt response) is closed by the main loop when it has not ended exchange_watchdog_us after its start (Timer3 restarts at 0 each exchange): compare off, SS high, one trip counted; the FCU sees one missing frame (resync / timeout tick). Must exceed 1.5 x the exchange and stay below the tick minus the push floor (generator checks). Chosen value, not a measurement.

link.lora_uart_note: Ebyte E22/E220/E32-class: set channel, air rate (2.4 kbps assumed) and address with the vendor tool; M0 = M1 = 0 for normal (transparent) mode
link.frequency_note: Korea: KC-certified module in the 920 MHz band (920.9-923.3 MHz used here for sx127x); 433 MHz legality not verified - check rra.go.kr

flight_computer.architecture_v081: v0.8.1 (architect 2026-10-21 20:30, after the v0.8 integration measured the 3-chip GPS build: NAV mandatory work 98.7 % mean / 119.5 % max of the 4 ms tick, FCU time-critical 83.3 % (89.2 % with ISRs), FCU background starved (no ilink CMD decoded in position hold -> V1 LAND), FCU stack free 436 B, IMU->vane up to 16.4 ms; the no-GPS v0.8 build passes timing): FOUR ATmega128A. GNS (GPS navigation + station keeping) = a 4th board: NEO-6M on its USART1 (PD2/PD3, 38400, level-shifted), UBX parsing, the GPS-aided horizontal filter (gps_nav) and the position controller (position_ctrl) at 50 Hz; NAV keeps the attitude / altitude estimators (the passing no-GPS v0.8 load) and links to the GNS over glink; the FCU no longer runs the position controller (RAM / background back to the no-GPS build) and takes the tilt setpoint + GPS status from the nlink rotating slot that the NAV fills from the GNS. Every flight computation stays on ATmega128A boards.

gns.role: GNS: GPS receiver driver + UBX + gps_nav filter + position controller (50 Hz); no safety decisions (the FCU supervisor keeps V11-V15 on the slot data)
